_help: English is the source catalog. Keys are grouped by system; placeholders are ICU MessageFormat: {name}, {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}}, {gender, select, feminine {...} masculine {...} other {...}}. Apostrophes are plain text. SQL keywords, table and column names stay in English in every language.

miscast.gibberish: {player.name}: Mmm that was NOT the right way of making the spell.
miscast.one_at_a_time: {player.name}: Hahaha no. Put the semicolon down: one spell per cast, or one BEGIN ... COMMIT block.
miscast.not_understood: {player.name}: That's not a spell the Grimoire knows. It looked at it, sighed, and closed itself.
miscast.forgery: {player.name}: Ink cannot conjure names. Pick them from a table.
miscast.attach: {player.name}: ATTACH another database? Absolutely not. We have enough monsters here.
miscast.detach: {player.name}: DETACH? Nothing here is attached, and nothing will be.
miscast.vacuum: Grimoire: VACUUM? I am a book, not a broom.
miscast.pragma: Grimoire: *Angry noises*. Only a few PRAGMAs are allowed: table_info, table_list, index_list, index_info, foreign_key_list.
miscast.too_slow: {player.name}: That spell collapsed under its own weight. The grimoire is still smoking.
miscast.too_big: Grimoire: My pages are full. Whatever you were building, it is too big for this world.
miscast.denied: Grimoire: That reaches outside the world. Some doors stay shut, even for witches.
miscast.not_understood_error: {player.name}: The world does not understand that. ({error})
miscast.duplicate_name: Grimoire: There is already something called {name} in this world. Names are unique here, or spells would not know whom to hit.
miscast.witch_row: Grimoire: You are not a row I will let you delete.
miscast.transaction_left_open: Grimoire: You opened a transaction and never closed it. I tore that page out (ROLLBACK).

world.rage: {foe} is enraged: its spells hit harder until the world is put back.
world.confused_end: The fight dissolves into confusion. There is nothing left to win.

reaction.drop_spells: Hahaha! Your spellbook is gone, witch. Now I can hit you as hard as I like.
reaction.empty_spells: Not a single spell left? This will be quick.
reaction.drop_foe_spells: My book... where is my book? I cannot remember a single spell.
reaction.empty_foe_spells: Every page of my book is blank. What did you do?
reaction.delete_foe_row: I... am not in the enemies table any more. Am I still here?
reaction.drop_enemies: There are no enemies any more. Not even me. What is this fight about?
reaction.delete_witch_row: You are not a row I will let you delete.
reaction.drop_witch: You are not a table I will let you drop.
reaction.drop_items: Your satchel just fell into the void. Gone, all of it.
reaction.drop_type_chart: Fire, water, storm... it is all the same now. Nothing is strong against anything.
reaction.rename_foe_column: The words in my book have moved. I can no longer read my own spells!
reaction.alter_spells: You rewrote your own spells? Cheating, witch. I can cheat too.
reaction.insert_spell: A spell from nowhere. Clever. I will remember that.
reaction.core_lookalike: A table that looks like {table}? I will not be fooled... I think.
reaction.rollback_no_transaction: ROLLBACK what? There is nothing to undo. You have to BEGIN first.
reaction.commit: COMMIT. Done is done: there is no ROLLBACK for that any more.
reaction.rewind: Back again, are we? Time is a page you can turn, it seems.
reaction.rewind_grimoire: I turned the world back to turn {turn}. It cost you this turn.

trick.shadow_book: Wait... that is not my book. It is your view of my book! Well played, witch.
trick.read_my_mind: You read my own query from query_log before I cast it again? Clever.

codex.acknowledged: {foe}: You already know {technique}? Then show me.

WHERE.title: WHERE: ask only for what you need
WHERE.text: WHERE keeps the rows that pass a test: WHERE element = 'Fire'.

ORDER BY.title: ORDER BY: put rows in order
ORDER BY.text: ORDER BY power DESC puts the strongest first.
ORDER BY.dialects: Same everywhere; NULLs sort first in SQLite and MySQL, last in PostgreSQL.

LIMIT.title: LIMIT: only the first rows
LIMIT.text: LIMIT 1 keeps one row: cast one spell, pay for one spell.
LIMIT.dialects: PostgreSQL and MySQL: LIMIT too. SQL Server: TOP; the SQL standard: FETCH FIRST.

JOIN.title: JOIN: match two tables
JOIN.text: JOIN puts rows of two tables side by side when a condition matches.
JOIN.dialects: Same; SQLite has no RIGHT or FULL JOIN before version 3.39.

GROUP BY.title: GROUP BY: one row per group
GROUP BY.text: GROUP BY element, with COUNT(*), counts the spells of each element.
GROUP BY.dialects: PostgreSQL is stricter: every selected column must be grouped or aggregated.

HAVING.title: HAVING: filter the groups
HAVING.text: HAVING COUNT(*) > 2 keeps the groups with more than two rows.

DISTINCT.title: DISTINCT: no repeats
DISTINCT.text: SELECT DISTINCT element lists each element once.

SUBQUERY.title: Subqueries: an answer inside an answer
SUBQUERY.text: WHERE power > (SELECT AVG(power) FROM spells) compares with a computed value.

WITH.title: WITH: name a step
WITH.text: WITH strong AS (SELECT ...) SELECT ... FROM strong reads like a recipe.

IS NULL.title: IS NULL: the missing value
IS NULL.text: NULL is not equal to anything, not even NULL: test it with IS NULL.

COALESCE.title: COALESCE: a value instead of nothing
COALESCE.text: COALESCE(hp, 0) gives 0 when hp is NULL.
COALESCE.dialects: Same; MySQL also has IFNULL, SQL Server ISNULL.

UNION.title: UNION: one list from two
UNION.text: SELECT name FROM spells UNION SELECT name FROM items joins two results, without repeats.
UNION.dialects: Same; UNION ALL keeps the repeats.

EXCEPT.title: EXCEPT: what one has and the other lacks
EXCEPT.text: The rows of the first result that are not in the second.

INTERSECT.title: INTERSECT: what both share
INTERSECT.text: The rows that appear in both results.

INSERT.title: INSERT: bring something into the world
INSERT.text: INSERT INTO items (name, kind, amount, qty) VALUES (...) adds a row.
INSERT.dialects: Same; PostgreSQL adds RETURNING, SQLite has it too since 3.35.

UPDATE.title: UPDATE: correct the world
UPDATE.text: UPDATE ... SET ... WHERE ... changes rows. Forget the WHERE and you change them all.

DELETE.title: DELETE: let go, carefully
DELETE.text: DELETE FROM ... WHERE ... removes rows. Without WHERE it removes every row.
DELETE.dialects: Same; TRUNCATE in PostgreSQL and MySQL empties a table faster.

DROP.title: DROP: remove a whole table
DROP.text: DROP TABLE removes the table and everything in it. Only a backup brings it back.
DROP.dialects: Same; PostgreSQL can undo it inside a transaction.

CREATE TABLE.title: CREATE TABLE: a new place for data
CREATE TABLE.text: CREATE TABLE notes (text TEXT) makes an empty table.
CREATE TABLE.dialects: Types are strict in PostgreSQL, loose in SQLite.

CREATE VIEW.title: CREATE VIEW: a saved question
CREATE VIEW.text: A view is a query with a name; reading it runs the query. Your Scrolls are views.

CREATE INDEX.title: CREATE INDEX: find rows fast
CREATE INDEX.text: An index is a sorted copy of a column, so searches do not read every row.
CREATE INDEX.dialects: Same; each database chooses when to use it.

CREATE TRIGGER.title: CREATE TRIGGER: a trap in the data
CREATE TRIGGER.text: A trigger runs its own statements when rows are inserted, updated or deleted.
CREATE TRIGGER.dialects: PostgreSQL triggers call a function; MySQL's look like SQLite's.

ALTER.title: ALTER TABLE: reshape a table
ALTER.text: ALTER TABLE spells RENAME COLUMN power TO might renames a column.
ALTER.dialects: SQLite can rename, add and drop columns, little else.

TRANSACTION.title: Transactions: all or nothing
TRANSACTION.text: BEGIN ... COMMIT applies every statement or none; ROLLBACK undoes them.
TRANSACTION.dialects: Same; MySQL needs the InnoDB engine.

PRAGMA.title: PRAGMA: ask the database about itself
PRAGMA.text: PRAGMA table_info(spells) lists the columns of a table.
PRAGMA.dialects: SQLite only: PostgreSQL uses information_schema, MySQL uses DESCRIBE.

backups.title: Backups: the world you can return to
backups.text: You broke the world and did not rewind. A backup (a snapshot) is how real systems survive mistakes like that.
backups.dialects: sqlite3 .backup; pg_dump in PostgreSQL; mysqldump in MySQL.

trickster.title: Trickster: knowledge beats force
trickster.text: You broke a guardian with what you know about databases. That counts.

insight.title: Looking first
insight.text: Before writing anything, an analyst reads the shape of the data: which tables exist, which columns they have, what a few rows look like. SELECT * FROM a table LIMIT 5 is the oldest habit in the trade. In battle every first look at a table pays a little MP.
insight.dialects: PostgreSQL and MySQL: the same. Their own catalogues (information_schema) list every table and column; SQLite keeps them in sqlite_master and PRAGMA table_info.

screen.title: CODEX: what you know, in your own queries
screen.empty: Nothing yet: every technique you use or see is written here.
screen.close: Any key: back to the battle

book_closed.foe_turn: The book is closed: it is {foe}'s turn.
book_closed.animating: The book is closed while the spell resolves.
book_closed.over: The book is closed: the fight is over.

rewind.title: REWIND (F6): turn the world back
rewind.help: UP/DOWN choose, ENTER rewind (costs this turn), F6/ESC close
rewind.empty: Nothing to rewind yet: every change you make is saved here first.

scroll.saved: Scroll saved: {name}. Cast it with SELECT * FROM {name}.
scroll.bad_name: A Scroll's name uses letters, digits and _ only, up to 24 characters.

battle.margin: {count, plural, one {# spell fizzles} other {# spells fizzle}} in the margin
battle.relevance_up: Ward of Relevance is up: only super-effective spells pass

fatigue.focus: Clean casts. Focus: one more row.

battle.hourglass: {spell}: the next Rewind costs no turn.
battle.free_rewind: The Hourglass turns. Your turn goes on.

panel.tables_title: TABLES  (click a name to write it)
panel.tables_rule: A row with a 'name' from spells or items casts it. The rest is a free look.

grimoire.footer: CTRL+ENTER cast TAB complete F3 guide F6 rewind

title.subtitle: a turn-based RPG where your queries are spells

result.fainted: {player.name} sways; the ink swims. You wake by the fire.

guide._help: The spell guide's frame (F3). Its pages are data/guide.json (keys guide.<path>).
guide.title: SPELL GUIDE
guide.keys: <- -> pages   UP/DOWN choose   ENTER write it on the page   F3/ESC close
guide.runes_intro: Runes are SQL keywords. You learn each one from the guardian
guide.runes_intro2: who uses it: watch its book, then copy it.

speaker._help: Names shown on a speaker's tag. Guardians use their names from the database (data, in English); the Grimoire and the protagonist are translated here.

menu._help: The title and system screens (engine/menus.py). at.*: where a save stands, shown in the Load list.
menu.damaged_backup: (damaged: ENTER loads the last good copy)
menu.no_saves: (no saves yet: ENTER starts its story)
menu.delete_hint: ENTER play   DEL delete a profile   ESC back
menu.confirm_delete: Delete {name} and every save? ENTER deletes, ESC keeps it.

consent.title: Help us make the game better?
consent.text: If you agree, the game sends anonymous notes about how battles go: which techniques you use (SELECT, WHERE...), how long a lesson takes, when hints appear. Never your name, never what you type, never anything that identifies you. It is off unless you say yes, and you can change it any time in Settings.

settings._help: The settings screen (engine/settings.py). row.*: the name of each setting; value.*: a setting's value in words.
settings.title: SETTINGS
settings.keys: UP/DOWN choose   LEFT/RIGHT change   ENTER rebind a key   ESC back

stats.title: STATISTICS
stats.keys: LEFT/RIGHT pages   R this run / all   E export   ESC back

creator.title: WHO ARE YOU, WITCH?
creator.keys: UP/DOWN choose   LEFT/RIGHT change   type your name   ENTER on Done

name.empty: Grimoire: A witch needs a name. How about {suggestion}?
name.too_long: Grimoire: Twelve letters at most, or it will not fit on my pages. {suggestion}?
name.characters: Grimoire: Quotes, backslashes and semicolons would break every spell that says your name. {suggestion}? (TAB)
name.taken: Grimoire: That name is already something in this world, and names here are unique. {suggestion}? (TAB)
name.keyword: Grimoire: That is a word of power, not a name: SQL would read it as a command. {suggestion}? (TAB)

shop.refuse: Look all you like, or put something in your items. I do not sell anything else.
shop.nothing: Your query put nothing in your items. Pick a row of the stall.
shop.not_for_sale: {name}? That is not on my stall. Copy the row from stall.

hearth.just_looking: A look at the pot. Name a recipe to cook it.
hearth.no_letters: The letter box is empty tonight.
